newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs sell steady-$0.50 lower -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs sell steady-$0.50 lower -dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices early Monday were mostly steady, instances $0.50 per cwt lower, amid light demand following last week's large marketings, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Packer operating margins were cut by the week's big pork production, which pushed pork prices lower.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota were $0.50 lower at $54.00, with country buying stations paying a top of $53.00, sources there said.
Illinois top prices at plants were reported at $53.00, with country points at $52.50.
Indiana and Ohio top plant prices ranged from $53.50 to $54.00, with interior tops ranging from $51.00 to $52.00.
Hog marketings reportedly were light early as producers held animals back in an attempt to force cash prices higher, dealers said.

However, hog weights were gradually creeping up amid mild weather in the Corn Belt, which has allowed for rapid weight gains. Weights also were up due to hogs already held back as producers concentrated on harvesting this fall. Average weights for the week ended Oct 19 was estimated at 253 lbs compared with 250 lbs previous week and 256.0 lbs last year, USDA said.
